At three in the morning, the car was filled with smoke, and at 38 years old, he stared at the dwindling over 3 million U#ETH  in his account, his voice trembling: "Brother Jie, I clearly made money before, why am I still a loser?"
I've seen this scene too many times. The common problems of retail investors are all present in him—impatience, greed, and fear of missing out. The cryptocurrency market never lacks opportunities; what it lacks is the ability to see through traps.
What are the main players best at? Creating dreams. When the coin price suddenly skyrockets, the group is filled with voices of "take off," and as you chase it, it starts to sharpen its knife. It falls and bounces back, and you think you’ve caught the bottom, but in fact, that’s just the main players’ final exit show. The real bottom is when someone quietly takes over, continuously increasing the volume, and the price stops falling.
I watch the market, first looking at the volume. High volume at high positions might indicate the market is not over; low volume at high positions means even the best story must come to an end. After nine years of trading, I’ve realized a principle: making money relies not on chasing, but on patience. Being patient not to buy randomly, being patient not to chase highs, and being patient to stay clear-headed during the frenzy, holding cash and waiting.
How many people lose money, not because they don't know how to buy, but because they can't control their hands, knowing it's a pit but still jumping in. I’ve survived until now, not because I’ve always made the right calls, but because I know when to stop.
The market is always there, but the capital can't withstand too many tosses. Follow Brother Jie, not to boast or brag, but to teach you how to minimize losses and how to slowly turn things around.
